name: Cua
description: Observe and operate native desktop applications, windows, and OS dialogs through Cua Driver. Use browser_use for websites.
progressive_guidance:
Extract exact text in this order: accessibility text, the source app's Copy action with copy_text, then OCR only if neither works. After locating the source, inspect accessibility or its context menu before transcribing links. Empty accessibility is not a failed Copy attempt; zoom can help target Copy but is not the first text-extraction step.
Use current observations: window images establish window pixels; desktop/menu images establish desktop pixels. Pass attached-image pixels directly, including zoom crops; Leon maps them. Element tokens require the latest matching window snapshot; element_index also requires snapshot_id.
Respect the configured interaction mode. Visible mode forces foreground input; background support depends on the target. Remember background_unavailable and retry foreground only when permitted. Input returns a final observation by default: reuse it, and inspect uncertain delivery before retrying. Dispatch success is not proof of the intended effect. Resolve a modal using its own target before returning to the parent.
Resolve item identity before changing a collection; do not add/remove candidates merely to inspect them. Preserve verified outcomes and update the existing plan at verified milestones. Identify field meaning before editing and verify resulting values; ask about unresolved choices and preserve no-submit constraints. Playback controls must be verified against actual playback state, not a title or stationary progress position.

list_apps.description: List installed desktop applications and configured preferred_apps. Use it to choose a launch target when the owner did not name one.
list_apps.progressive_guidance: preferred_apps includes saved choices even when query filters the app list. found_in_desktop_inventory=false means no desktop entry matched, not that the app is absent: for a terminal-hosted app, consult ACTIVITY.md process ancestry and inspect the host's correct idle session. The terminal is its host, not a replacement for the selected app. Running time is not proof of preference. Remote context must describe the target device, not the server. Save a new preference only with owner confirmation.

query.description: Optional case-insensitive app name, bundle ID, or launch-path substring.

list_windows.description: List a compact set of native desktop windows. Use this before launching when the request may continue in an existing workspace. Filter by pid when the destination process is already known, and use on_screen_only when only visible windows matter.

on_screen_only.description: When true, filter to visible windows only. Default false.

z_index.description: Higher values are closer to the front. Null means the provider cannot observe stacking order; callers must not infer an order from array position or treat null as zero.

health_report.description: Diagnose driver, permissions, accessibility, and screenshot capabilities after a concrete failure. Read the reported checks and remediation hints; do not run routinely before healthy actions.

include.description: Omit on the first diagnostic call to run all checks. To filter later, copy exact checks[].name values from a previous report; do not invent category names. Wins over skip.

skip.description: Skip these checks (canonical names). Ignored when `include` is set.

get_window_state.description: Inspect one native window and return its interface tree plus a screenshot. Use this for visible appearance, colors, or controls after list_windows.
get_window_state.progressive_guidance: Use the returned accessibility text before Copy or OCR. If only the outer frame is exposed, retry the tree at most once for a missing control. Reuse the latest post-action observation; additions/removals can shift controls. For a loading destination, set settle_ms and observe rather than repeating navigation. Inspect newly opened windows/dialogs before restoring the previous window.

include_screenshot.description: Default true — returns a grounding screenshot alongside the tree. Set false to skip the grab and return tree only (the cheap path for re-indexing before an element ax action).

max_depth.description: Optional traversal-depth override. Omit for Leon's bounded default: modern applications can nest useful controls dozens of levels deep. Use a smaller limit only for a deliberately shallow inspection.

max_elements.description: Optional override for the cap on accessibility nodes walked. Omit for Leon's bounded default. Increase only when a needed control is omitted; query filters results without reducing traversal cost.

query.description: Optional case-insensitive substring. Projects both tree_markdown and structured elements to matches plus ancestors while preserving original indices. Compare total_element_count with returned_element_count.

settle_ms.description: Optional bounded wait before observing a loading or transitioning interface. Does not repeat input or guarantee readiness. Omit for an immediate observation.

zoom.description: Enlarge a region of the latest screenshot for precise targeting or reading after accessibility and Copy fail. Returns a crop with mapped input coordinates.
zoom.progressive_guidance: Match the latest screenshot: scope=desktop for desktop/menu images, otherwise supply its pid/window_id. Inspect the crop before acting with its pixels and capture_target; never calculate offsets or convert them back to desktop/window coordinates, including inside copy_text. Never batch zoom with a dependent click. Observe the full target before another zoom. Reading zoom follows accessibility and an actual Copy attempt; targeting zoom can help locate a small Copy control.

pid.description: Process owning the observed window. Omit for desktop zoom.

x1.description: Rectangle coordinate in the latest full desktop or window image, matching scope.

x2.description: Rectangle coordinate in the latest full desktop or window image, matching scope.

y1.description: Rectangle coordinate in the latest full desktop or window image, matching scope.

y2.description: Rectangle coordinate in the latest full desktop or window image, matching scope.

purpose.description: act: crop for controls. read: clean PNG crop for reading, enlarged up to 2x. Both support input in crop pixels with the returned capture_target. Neither is a fresh capture.

scope.description: Match the observed image: desktop for get_desktop_state or a context-menu screenshot (omit pid/window_id), window for get_window_state (supply pid/window_id).

verify_state.description: Deterministically verify a concrete task postcondition after an action. Do not call this merely to confirm that an unrelated target window still exists.
verify_state.progressive_guidance: Verify a concrete expected semantic condition after an action. For loading or blank destinations without a known condition, observe with get_window_state/get_desktop_state and settle_ms instead; do not replay navigation.

expect.description: One to eight predicates, combined with AND. Example: {"element":{"selector":{"role":"button","label_contains":"Play"},"exists":true}}. Put role/label_contains inside selector, not beside exists.

exists.description: Set true to assert that at least one trusted element matches the selector.

selector.description: Element selector. Provide role or label_contains.

bounds.description: Expected bounds. Provide x, y, width, and height; tolerance_px is optional.

include_screenshot.description:
Return the final window screenshot as image content for a multimodal
caller. The driver does not interpret that image.

pid.description: Exact process whose window may be observed.

stable_samples.description: Consecutive satisfied samples required before returning success.

timeout_ms.description: Bounded wait. Zero performs one sample.

get_desktop_state.description: Capture the visible desktop without an accessibility-tree walk. Use for current context, controls outside one window, or recovery after ineffective window actions.
get_desktop_state.progressive_guidance: Use for visible context and controls outside one window, or recovery after ineffective window capture/input. For exact text or URLs, next inspect accessibility or the source's Copy action rather than transcribing the screenshot. A desktop capture establishes desktop coordinates, not window coordinates.

settle_ms.description: Optional bounded wait before observing a loading or transitioning interface. Does not repeat input or guarantee readiness. Omit for an immediate observation.

move_cursor.description: Move the desktop pointer to reveal a hover menu or tooltip without clicking.
move_cursor.progressive_guidance: Use a visible, unobscured target from the latest desktop screenshot and only when foreground interaction is permitted. Set capture_after=true to inspect the revealed tooltip/menu.

x.description: Horizontal pixel coordinate in the latest attached desktop image.

y.description: Vertical pixel coordinate in the latest attached desktop image.

capture_after.description: Capture the resulting desktop state after moving the pointer.

settle_ms.description: Optional wait after input and before the post-action capture, in milliseconds. Use for expected navigation or delayed dialogs. Requires capture_after=true; input is delivered only once.

launch_app.description: Launch the chosen desktop application by name, bundle ID, or path.
launch_app.progressive_guidance: Continue in a relevant existing window before launching. Use the observed launch_path from list_apps when available. URLs use the OS default handler independently; put the URL in additional_arguments when the selected app matters. Inspect the new window before acting.

additional_arguments.description: Extra command-line arguments passed to the exact launched application. Use browser_use to navigate webpages in the owner's existing browser session.

launch_path.description: Round-trip the `launch_path` returned by `list_apps` — the Exec= command from the .desktop file with XDG field codes already stripped. Highest precedence on Linux; spawned directly via the system shell.

name.description: App name or command to launch. Tried as a direct command first, then matched against installed .desktop applications (exact display name, desktop-file id, or Exec basename; else an unambiguous display-name substring).

urls.description: URLs opened through the OS default handler, independently of launch_path or name. Do not use this when an exact browser was selected.

bring_to_front.description: Bring a known window forward when persistent visibility or desktop interaction is needed.
bring_to_front.progressive_guidance: Use only for persistent visibility or an exposed desktop target. Ordinary foreground input already activates its target and normally restores prior focus; foreground right-clicks keep the target in front so the menu remains available.

window_id.description: X11 window id (xid) to activate. If omitted, the first window of `pid` is used.

invoke_menu.description: Invoke an observed native application-menu path in one call.
invoke_menu.progressive_guidance: Use an exact observed application-menu path. The driver handles activation and restoration; a separate bring_to_front is unnecessary. Inspect the result rather than treating delivery as completion.

parameters.description:
Exact, immediate-child application menu path to resolve and invoke through
the operating system's accessibility API. Path labels are matched after
trimming surrounding whitespace and otherwise remain case-sensitive.

click.description: Click a current semantic element or a control in the latest matching screenshot.
click.progressive_guidance: Locate the control in the latest matching screenshot or use its current semantic token. After layout changes, re-locate the target instead of reusing old pixels. If a small target is uncertain, inspect a zoom first and pass crop pixels directly. For Copy, use copy_text to verify the clipboard. Inspect an opened context menu before choosing its item. Open dropdowns only for needed choices; retry only when new evidence changes the failure mode.

capture_after.description: Return a fresh observation after input (default true). For a batch, capture only after its final action.

button.description: Mouse button. Default: "left" (legacy back-compat). X11: routed via ButtonPress/Release with the matching evdev code. Native Wayland: only left-button is supported via the virtual-pointer protocol; right/middle return an error.

delivery_mode.description: Choose background (default) or foreground delivery. Follow the tool guidance and returned diagnostics.

element_index.description: Element index from get_window_state; pass its matching snapshot_id. Prefer element_token.

element_token.description: Element handle from the latest get_window_state for the same target.

modifier.description: Modifier keys held during the action: cmd, shift, option/alt, ctrl.

target.description: Exact window or desktop target returned by a state call.

settle_ms.description: Optional wait after input and before the post-action capture, in milliseconds. Use for expected navigation or delayed dialogs. Requires capture_after=true; input is delivered only once.

drag.description: Drag between two screenshot coordinates in one target window.

capture_after.description: Return a fresh observation after input (default true). For a batch, capture only after its final action.

delivery_mode.description: Choose background (default) or foreground delivery. Follow the tool guidance and returned diagnostics.

modifier.description: Modifier keys held during the action: cmd, shift, option/alt, ctrl.

target.description: Exact window or desktop target returned by a state call.

settle_ms.description: Optional wait after input and before the post-action capture, in milliseconds. Use for expected navigation or delayed dialogs. Requires capture_after=true; input is delivered only once.

scroll.description: Scroll a target window or UI element in one direction.
scroll.progressive_guidance: Survey long content in one direction with page-sized scrolls and capture_after=true. Reuse observations and stop at the end, repeated content, or sufficient evidence; state remaining uncertainty.

capture_after.description: Return a fresh observation after input (default true). For a batch, capture only after its final action.

delivery_mode.description: Choose background (default) or foreground delivery. Follow the tool guidance and returned diagnostics.

element_index.description: Element index from get_window_state; pass its matching snapshot_id. Prefer element_token.

element_token.description: Element handle from the latest get_window_state for the same target.

target.description: Exact window or desktop target returned by a state call.

x.description: Window-local screenshot-pixel X of the scroll target. Pass with y and without element_index.

y.description: Window-local screenshot-pixel Y of the scroll target. Pass with x and without element_index.

settle_ms.description: Optional wait after input and before the post-action capture, in milliseconds. Use for expected navigation or delayed dialogs. Requires capture_after=true; input is delivered only once.

type_text.description: Type into a field; use mode=replace to focus once, select all and replace its value. Inspect the returned observation to verify the result.
type_text.progressive_guidance: For exact, multilingual or multiline field values, prefer method=paste using Cua's clipboard; it replaces clipboard text. Use mode=replace to focus once and replace the field value. Verify the returned observation before continuing. If input is partial or unchanged, inspect focus before retrying; do not append another copy or create shell clipboard helpers.

method.description: type (default) uses driver typing; paste writes clipboard text and pastes once into the target. Paste replaces the current clipboard contents.

capture_after.description: Return a fresh observation after input (default true). For a batch, capture only after its final action.

delivery_mode.description: Choose background (default) or foreground delivery. Follow the tool guidance and returned diagnostics.

element_index.description: Element index from get_window_state; pass its matching snapshot_id. Prefer element_token.

element_token.description: Element handle from the latest get_window_state for the same target.

target.description: Exact window or desktop target returned by a state call.

x.description: Screenshot-pixel X of the field to type into — the element px action form. Pass x,y (no element_index) and the tool pixel-clicks there to establish real renderer focus, then types. Use for Chromium/Electron inputs the AX path can't reach. Read straight off the get_window_state PNG, same convention as click. For replacement use mode=replace. After a separate focus/select-all sequence, omit x/y to preserve selection.

y.description: Screenshot-pixel Y of the field (see x).

settle_ms.description: Optional wait after input and before the post-action capture, in milliseconds. Use for expected navigation or delayed dialogs. Requires capture_after=true; input is delivered only once.

mode.description: insert types at the caret. replace selects all in the established field before typing; x/y or a current element handle focuses it once. Without a field selector, uses the already focused field.

press_key.description: Press one key, with optional modifiers, in a target window.

capture_after.description: Return a fresh observation after input (default true). For a batch, capture only after its final action.

delivery_mode.description: Choose background (default) or foreground delivery. Follow the tool guidance and returned diagnostics.

element_index.description: Element index from get_window_state; pass its matching snapshot_id. Prefer element_token.

element_token.description: Element handle from the latest get_window_state for the same target.

key.description: Canonical lowercase CUA key name. Use `return` to submit or commit, not `enter`; common names include `tab`, `escape`, `space`, `up`, `down`, `left`, `right`, `home`, `end`, `pageup`, `pagedown`, and `delete`. Letters, digits, and function keys use their lowercase form.

target.description: Exact window or desktop target returned by a state call.

x.description: Screenshot-pixel X — the element px action form: pixel-click there to focus, then send the key. Use when the key must go to a Chromium/Electron surface the AX path can't focus. Pass with y, no element_index.

settle_ms.description: Optional wait after input and before the post-action capture, in milliseconds. Use for expected navigation or delayed dialogs. Requires capture_after=true; input is delivered only once.

hotkey.description: Press a key combination in a target window.
hotkey.progressive_guidance: Inspect unfamiliar application/editor shortcut help before acting. Confirm the intended field or control has focus; a selection shortcut on page content may select rows instead of text.

capture_after.description: Return a fresh observation after input (default true). For a batch, capture only after its final action.

delivery_mode.description: Choose background (default) or foreground delivery. Follow the tool guidance and returned diagnostics.

element_index.description: Element index from get_window_state; pass its matching snapshot_id. Prefer element_token.

element_token.description: Element handle from the latest get_window_state for the same target.

keys.description: Canonical lowercase CUA names for modifier(s) plus one non-modifier key, e.g. ["ctrl","c"]. Use `return` rather than `enter`.

target.description: Exact window or desktop target returned by a state call.

x.description: Screenshot-pixel X — the element px action form: pixel-click there to focus, then send the combo (so e.g. Ctrl+V pastes into that field). Pass with y. Use for Chromium/Electron surfaces the background combo can't reach.

settle_ms.description: Optional wait after input and before the post-action capture, in milliseconds. Use for expected navigation or delayed dialogs. Requires capture_after=true; input is delivered only once.

perform_actions.description: Run up to eight grounded inputs in order, stopping on failure. Use predictable steps that do not need intermediate visual decisions.
perform_actions.progressive_guidance: Batch predictable steps without intermediate visual decisions, with at most one pixel-targeted click. Within one field, combine click, select-all and type_text; do not batch different spatial fields or zoom with its dependent click. Set settle_ms on the last step before a navigation capture. Reuse the final observation and inspect uncertain input before retrying; capture_after=false is only for cases needing no observation.

capture_after.description: Return a fresh observation after input (default true). For a batch, capture only after its final action.

steps.description: Ordered mechanical actions. Each parameters object uses its action's schema. Include an explicit target on every keyboard step, even when reusing an already focused field; targets are not inherited from previous steps.

set_value.description: Set the value of an editable UI element from the latest window state.
set_value.progressive_guidance: Use a current editable element from get_window_state. Confirm the field's label and meaning, then verify the resulting value, units and dependent totals rather than relying on dispatch success.

element_index.description: Element index from get_window_state; pass its matching snapshot_id. Prefer element_token.

element_token.description: Element handle from the latest get_window_state for the same target.

window_id.description: Required when element_index is used; optional when element_token is supplied (the token carries it).

copy_text.description: Invoke an observed Copy action or selection shortcut and check the clipboard for exact source text. Prefer this over separate input and clipboard_read calls.
copy_text.progressive_guidance: Open and inspect a source context menu first if needed. Use an observed Copy/Copy link control or selection shortcut, preferably a current semantic handle or exact menu path. Pixel input targets the Copy row's center in the latest matching screenshot; pass crop pixels directly without conversion. This combines input and clipboard verification: unchanged text is unverified, and changed text still needs comparison with the intended source. Never invoke an unrelated action through copy_text.

window_id.description: Window owning the source text, even when its Copy menu needs a desktop-targeted click.

parameters.description: The observed Copy action's normal parameters, including its explicit target and fresh semantic handle or image coordinates. A popup may require a desktop target distinct from the source window.

clipboard_read.description: Read the current desktop clipboard; this does not prove a preceding Copy action succeeded.
clipboard_read.progressive_guidance: Prefer copy_text for extracting exact source text. If inspecting the clipboard separately, use include_text=true; reading successfully does not prove a Copy succeeded because the contents may be stale.

include_text.description:
Return plain-text clipboard content in addition to the available types.
Clipboard content is privacy-sensitive and is never retained in telemetry.

clipboard_write.description: Write text, an image, or a file to the desktop clipboard.

file_path.description: Absolute path to a local file to place on the clipboard as a file URL.

image_path.description: Absolute path to a local image to place on the clipboard.

text.description: Plain text to place on the clipboard.

start_recording.description: Start a host-managed computer-use recording for the current conversation.

record_video.description: Capture the main display to <output_dir>/recording.mp4. Default: false. Set to true to also capture the main display to recording.mp4 (otherwise only the per-turn screenshots + JSON are recorded). On macOS this uses native ScreenCaptureKit (no extra TCC prompt, macOS 15.0+); on Windows + Linux it requires ffmpeg on PATH.

stop_recording.description: Stop and finalize the active computer-use recording.
